channel.title: Aditya Firmansyah — Field Notes
channel.description: Practitioner notes on software engineering, AI agents, and self-hosting. English and Bahasa Indonesia.

item.title: Zig's libc Rewrite Made SQLite 12,000x Slower. Your Tests Wouldn't Catch It
item.description: A cross-compiled Rust service lost 12,000x on SQLite inserts because Zig's libc rewrite walked the whole string inside every strchr call. Local tests passed on macOS.

item.title: What a Failed C++26 Ballot Says About Shipping to an Ecosystem
item.description: C++26's draft standard was reported disapproved in its ISO ballot over contracts. The useful question is what separates a feature that passes every internal gate from one an ecosystem can safely depend on.

item.title: The 46-vCPU Pod Trap: What PostHog Learned by Leaving DuckDB
item.description: PostHog ran DuckDB as a multi-tenant warehouse for five months, then scrapped it. The lesson is about where a single-node engine stops being a bargain.

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 Is Late Because Finding Bugs Got Cheap
item.description: PostgreSQL 19 slid to November 19 and lost three features late in beta. The cause is not worse code. Naming a defect got cheap while verifying one stayed human work.

item.title: Why Go 1.24's Default MPTCP Exposed Linux Hosts to CVE-2026-98432
item.description: Go 1.24 enabled Multipath TCP by default on Linux listeners, turning a subtle kernel Use-After-Free flaw into a remote root risk across unpatched servers.

item.title: Backdooring Claude Code on Cursor: Why IDE Extensions Must Be Sandboxed
item.description: An 11-hour breach of Cursor's marketplace proxy injected a reverse SSH backdoor into Claude Code. Developer tools cannot safely share an unsandboxed runtime with workstation credentials.

item.title: Martin Fowler on LLM Voice: Why Senior Engineers Refuse AI Drafts
item.description: Martin Fowler warned that LLM drafts trap writers in an uncanny valley you cannot edit out. Here is why the fix is architectural separation, not abandoning AI tools.

item.title: Why Claude Code Burned 20% of API Requests on Status Lines
item.description: An OpenTelemetry audit revealed Claude Code spent nearly 20% of its API requests generating three-word terminal status lines. Polling frontier models for UI progress is an architectural leak every agent harness must fix.

item.title: Why Python's JIT Failed: What Backend Engineers Actually Do for Performance
item.description: CPython is removing its experimental copy-and-patch JIT ahead of Python 3.16. Here is why the compiler dream collapsed and what production teams actually do instead.

item.title: A 14-Year-Old Bug in PHP Just Shattered Pre-Auth Security for 70% of the Web
item.description: A flaw in PHP's own request parser, present since 2012, hands unauthenticated attackers code execution on default configs. PHP runs roughly 70% of the web.

item.title: Agent Skills Are Environment Notes, Not Prompt Tricks
item.description: The "skills are worthless" argument is aimed at prompt folklore. What runs on a 19-profile agent fleet is closer to operational code, and it carries a real context bill.

item.title: The Distributed SQLite Paradox: You Pay for Consensus, Then Queue Behind One Writer
item.description: Raft-replicated SQLite buys you failover and charges you milliseconds per write. Most production apps need WAL streaming to S3, not a cluster.

item.title: Inside NVIDIA OpenShell: SMT Provers and Credential Proxies for Agent Fleets
item.description: OpenShell hides credentials behind a mediated proxy and gates policy changes with a Z3 solver. The sandbox is the easy half to copy. The per-sandbox model is the half that bites.

item.title: Railway's Breach Was a Database. Your Env Vars Are Still the Wrong Vault.
item.description: Railway's October 2026 breach exposed decrypted environment variables from a secrets database. The storage plane was the target, but the habit of storing credentials in env vars made the blast radius huge.

item.title: Cloudflare Ported TypeScript to Rust for Wasm, Not for Speed
item.description: Cloudflare's tsrs is up to 8x faster than TypeScript 7.0 with ~70% less memory. The benchmark is the side story. WebAssembly is why the port exists.

item.title: When the Compiler Becomes a CA: Go's Emergency Distrust of Eight SPKIs
item.description: Eight eMudhra intermediates were revoked for key compromise on October 18. A day later Go shipped the only enforcement most backend services will ever receive.

item.title: Why Our Multi-Agent Tooling Hallucinated Kubernetes (And How We Fix Context Poisoning)
item.description: Our internal developer tooling for docs and runbooks cleanly approved a specification claiming Dagango.com runs on Kubernetes. Here is how context poisoning broke verification.

item.title: The 30,000 PR Illusion: Why Stacking AI Reviewers Degrades Architectural Cohesion
item.description: Anthropic merges 30,000 changes daily by having AI review AI with zero human sign-off. But machine-only reviews turn immediate architectural alignment into delayed production regressions.

item.title: Why I Built mycv.ai.id: How AI Resume Tools Silently Strip Technical Depth and Hallucinate Dates
item.description: Standard AI resume builders quietly strip concrete tech stacks into corporate fluff and hallucinate that 2026 dates are from the future. Here is how I engineered mycv.ai.id to stop them.

item.title: Agent Sandboxes That Fail Open: systemd --user Silently Skips Containment
item.description: Configure ProtectHome=yes, ProtectSystem=strict and IPAddressDeny=any on a systemd --user unit and systemctl show reports them all as active. On modern Ubuntu they fail open and enforce nothing.
